note: Each item is a 'symbol' the serpent can swallow; eating it reveals a fact. Every fact is drawn from real chapter text — 'basis' must appear in the source chapter (checked by tools/verify-ouroboros.js).

facts.label: The Ouroboros
facts.fact: The ouroboros, the serpent devouring its own tail, was taken up as an emblem of eternity and the unity of all things.

facts.label: The Devourer
facts.fact: In Egypt, Ammit — 'the Devourer' — crouched by the scales to eat any heart that weighed heavy with wrongdoing.

facts.label: The Ziggurat
facts.fact: Mesopotamia raised the ziggurat, a stepped temple-mountain, as a house for its gods.

facts.label: The Tree of Life
facts.fact: Kabbalah maps the hidden God as ten emanations (sefirot) arranged on the Tree of Life.

facts.label: The Fish
facts.fact: Early Christians hid a creed in a fish: the Greek 'ichthys' read as an acrostic for Jesus Christ, Son of God, Savior.

facts.label: Linear B
facts.fact: Deciphering Linear B revealed Greek gods' names already written in the Bronze Age.

facts.label: The Empty Throne
facts.fact: For three centuries early Buddhists depicted the Buddha by not depicting him — an empty throne, footprints, a wheel.

facts.label: Göbekli Tepe
facts.fact: Göbekli Tepe's carved pillars, older than farming, suggest the temple may have come before the city.

facts.label: The Undying Fire
facts.fact: A Zoroastrian Atash Behram, a 'Fire of Victory', is tended by hand and never allowed to go out.

facts.label: The Dead Sea Scrolls
facts.fact: In caves at Qumran, jars gave up the Dead Sea Scrolls — the oldest copies of the Hebrew Bible by a thousand years.

facts.label: The Völva's Grave
facts.fact: The Oseberg ship burial — two women, a staff, and seeds — may be the grave of a Norse seeress.

facts.label: The Fifth Sun
facts.fact: The Aztec held that the world had been created and destroyed five times, and needed blood to keep the sun moving.

facts.label: The Rope Through the Tongue
facts.fact: A carved lintel from Yaxchilán shows a Maya queen drawing a thorn-set rope through her own tongue in bloodletting.

facts.label: A Gospel Before Nag Hammadi
facts.fact: The Gnostic gospel Pistis Sophia surfaced in Europe about 160 years before the 1945 Nag Hammadi find.
